With a 5 inch casing and a specific capacity of 0.13 m3/h per m, casing storage controls the drawdown for the first 80 minutes (Schafer's rule); each step pumped for 50 minutes, entirely inside it. The Cooper-Jacob and Theis fits see the borehole emptying rather than the aquifer. No fit outside that period can be adopted, so the Cooper-Jacob value is adopted only as the best available and the Theis value is reported but not adopted.

No method fitted to standard (Cooper-Jacob 2.50 m2/day, its fitted window 5-50 minutes lies inside the 80-minute casing-storage period; Theis curve fit 2.50 m2/day, each 50-minute step lies inside the 80-minute casing-storage period). The Cooper-Jacob value of 2.50 m2/day is adopted as the best available, so the yield rests on a fit that does not meet it.

positions.geology: The site lies on the unit the USGS Geologic Map of Africa maps as Holocene (Qe). Bullom Group (Q, Tb), Miocene to Recent. Sands, clays, clayey sands and lignite over the coastal lowland; alluvium along the drainage. Intergranular, generally the best yields available without deep drilling. Shallow water tables mean the protective cover is thin, so siting must keep clear of latrines and surface drainage. The BGS Africa Groundwater Atlas classes the aquifer here as Unconsolidated intergranular aquifer - moderate to high productivity (tertiary-quaternary unconsolidated sediments). Groundwater potential depends on the thickness of the weathered zone and the degree of fracturing beneath it, which the soundings below resolve.

positions.geology: The site lies on the unit the USGS Geologic Map of Africa maps as Paleozoic Igneous (Pi). Freetown Layered Complex (Jf), Jurassic (about 193 Ma). Layered gabbro, norite and anorthosite; a basic to ultrabasic intrusion forming the Freetown peninsula hills. Massive and crystalline, with negligible primary porosity. The BGS Africa Groundwater Atlas classes the aquifer here as Igneous intrusive aquifer - low productivity (igneous intrusive). positions.geology: The site lies on the unit the USGS Geologic Map of Africa maps as Precambrian (pCm). Precambrian basement, chiefly Leonean granite (LG, Lg, PLg, LM, Er, Lkm, Lkt), Archaean to Palaeoproterozoic. Crystalline basement, but not one rock. Cross-tabbed against the bundled BGS hydrogeology on a 1.4 km national grid, 87% of this class is basement aquifer and 12% is consolidated sedimentary with fracture flow - the Rokel River Group belt through Port Loko, Kambia, Moyamba and Tonkolili. On the 2017 map the basement part is chiefly Leonean granite (LG), with Liberian granite (Lg), migmatitic gneiss (PLg, LM), the Magbele and Tapr formations (Lkm, Lkt) and a mylonite zone. Mostly the crystalline basement aquifer this toolkit is built for: no primary porosity, water in the weathered and fractured zone above fresh rock, yield following regolith thickness and the fracture set at the weathered-fresh contact. But this class is not one rock, and where it covers the Rokel River metasediments the aquifer is fracture flow in indurated beds with shales acting as aquicludes - a different target. Read the aquifer map beside it: the BGS layer separates the two where this one does not. The BGS Africa Groundwater Atlas classes the aquifer here as Basement aquifer - low productivity (precambrian craton). Groundwater potential depends on the thickness of the weathered zone and the degree of fracturing beneath it, which the soundings below resolve.

unplaced_geology.geology: The project area lies within the Freetown Basic Complex. The Freetown Complex is a layered gabbroic anorthosite intrusion emplaced against gneisses and schists of the Kasila Group, and it forms part of the Peninsula and Banana Islands. It is thought to have been formed by multiple injections of magma that occurred intermittently. Groundwater potential within the Freetown Basic Complex is found within weathered and fractured zones of these igneous (crystalline) rocks. Groundwater quality and quantity can be high if the borehole is properly located through appropriate hydrogeological and geophysical investigations.

The weathered zone develops on granites, gneisses and related rocks, and its thickness and degree of fracturing control the groundwater potential. Groundwater quality and quantity can be favourable where the borehole position is properly located through appropriate hydrogeological and geophysical investigations.

notes: Casing storage: if the transmissivity is as low as 1 m2/day, the water levels of the first 307 minutes may show the 5 inch casing, with its 1.25 inch riser, emptying rather than the aquifer (31 minutes at 10 m2/day).

Step test: run every step for at least 60 minutes, and the first for at least 307 minutes, since the drawdown is fitted on the first step.
A shorter test is safe only once the measured drawdown shows a shorter casing-storage time. The pumping test co-pilot or the office works that out from the discharge and the drawdown.

When the pump stops, start the clock again from zero and read the recovery at the same minutes.
sheets.discharge_note: Record the discharge of every step. Time a bucket of known volume three times; the rate in m3/h is 3.6 times the litres divided by the mean seconds. A step with no discharge is written as Not measured, with the reason.
